title: The Black Museum
paragraphs: Orson Welles narrates dramatizations of British murder cases, each introduced through an object preserved in Scotland Yard's Black Museum and used as the doorway into the crime story.

Syndicated true-crime radio anthology hosted and narrated by Orson Welles, using objects associated with cases from Scotland Yard's Black Museum as dramatic frames. The frozen GRH container preserves 32 of the circulating programs. Source logs explicitly warn that surviving titles, program numbers, and broadcast order vary; no episode-specific 1952 airdate is imposed.
GRH documents the program through 1952 U.S. Mutual/syndication circulation (January 1, 1952 to December 30, 1952) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Harry Alan Towers (producer on 32 recordings), Ira Marion (writer on 32 recordings), [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] (narrator on 32 recordings), and Sidney Torch (composer on 32 recordings and conductor on 32 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include crime-associated museum artifact, murder and homicide investigation, Scotland Yard and criminal investigation, forensic and physical evidence, clothing, textiles and personal effects, and documents, messages and written clues.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Scotland Yard Crime Museum case-artifact framing, International transcription syndication, Stable production team, and Title and order instability in syndicated preservation.
